milestone: M42 External Mode Pack Trust Expiry

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds runtime-owned signer trust expiry and makes approved candidate trust fail closed after the trust window ends.
Keeps expiry validation and approval denial in Rust runtime instead of VSIX policy.
Persists bounded trust expiry metadata without storing raw candidate/provenance data.
Gives scheduled callers deterministic fail-closed approval behavior when trusted signer authority has expired.

answers.strategic_capabilities: mode_pack_runtime with support from runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: modepack.trustSigner can record a bounded signer trust expiry, and modepack.approveCandidate treats an expired trusted signer as no longer current before writing approval state.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M41.1 can revoke signer trust, but unrevoked trust remains indefinite; there is no runtime-owned time boundary for temporary external Mode Pack publisher trust.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A trusted external signer can authorize candidates indefinitely unless a separate revoke action happens, which weakens autonomous recovery when trust should lapse automatically.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M40.1 trust creation, M41.1 revocation, and M39.2 provenance-gated approval because it adds time-bounded trust enforcement at approval time.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends the existing trustSigner input and approveCandidate enforcement path rather than adding a wrapper RPC.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds bounded expiry metadata to the existing trusted signer summary and no report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime validates future trust expiry on trust creation and rejects approval when the trusted signer snapshot has expired.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can set temporary signer trust and rely on fail-closed approval after expiry without a human cleanup step.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the minimal M42 trust-expiry vertical slice by adding trust-time validation, persisted expiry, replay-safe summary output, and approval enforcement.

exit_criteria: modepack.trustSigner records optional bounded signer expiry with explicit authorization
signer trust rejects malformed or already-expired expires_at values before writing trust state
signer trust replay returns the existing trusted signer entry including expiry without duplicate ModePackSignerTrusted events
modepack.approveCandidate re-reads current trusted signer expiry for the verified provenance signer before writing approved state
approval rejects expired trusted signer policy without writing approved candidate state
revoked signer denial remains fail-closed and is not bypassed by expiry handling
RPC and ledger payloads contain bounded metadata only and no raw candidate JSON, raw statement, raw signature bytes, or raw public key bytes
Behavior tests cover signer expiry mutation, expiry replay, expired trust denial, VSIX validation, and approval enforcement

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M42.1 changes signer trust expiry and approval behavior; review must confirm this is runtime trust enforcement, not a wrapper surface.
